Lauro Escorel | Lauro Escorel Filho (born January 5, 1950), most known as Lauro Escorel, is an American-born Brazilian cinematographer and film director. In 1978, he would win again the Gramado Film Festival Best Cinematography Award for his work on Héctor Babenco's "Lúcio Flávio, o Passageiro da Agonia". The story concerns the relationship of a homeless couple: Francis, an alcoholic, and Helen, a terminally ill woman during the Great Depression. After multiple commercials were filmed in the diner for Bounty paper towels with fictional character Rosie the Waitress, the diner was renamed Rosie's.  Previously offered to the Smithsonian Institution, the restaurant was sold in the 1990s to a Michigan artist who had the building moved to its current location next to another diner.  A third diner was later moved to the site from Fulton, New York.  A series of replicas were built as part of a chain of restaurants in the Denver area.

It was built from 1879 to 1883 at a cost of $627,148.  It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972.  It is also a contributing property to the Downtown Albany Historic District, listed on the Register in 1980.
Héctor Babenco | Héctor Eduardo Babenco (February 7, 1946July 13, 2016) was an Argentine-born Brazilian film director, screenwriter, producer and actor.  He worked in several countries including Argentina, Brazil and the United States.  His best known films are "Pixote" (1980), "Kiss of the Spider Woman" (1985), "Ironweed" (1987), "At Play in the Fields of the Lord" (1990) and "Carandiru" (2003).
